purpose: Audit trail for the money-type re-research. For eras 1, 5 and 7 it records, per pool: whether a source populates it or not, every estimation lens's central, the aggregation rule and the median it produced, the published interval and where its width comes from, the applied claim ID, and the grade. It also records each era's residual, the pairs the evidence cannot rank, every grade change, and the taxonomy question that is still open. Eras 2, 3, 4 and 6 were not re-researched at this stage and are untouched.
aggregation_rule: Headline is the plain median of the lens centrals. No extremizing anywhere: within each era the lenses share one evidence digest, so they are not informationally independent and extremizing can push the aggregate outside the panel (PROCESS.md rigor standard). Published interval = min lower bound to max upper bound across the lenses. No lens was discounted in any era. Routes sharing a common input were collapsed to one route before any weighting.
claim_id_policy: The four by_money_type claims in SCALE and BUYERS keep their existing IDs in all three eras; only their values, statements, methods, sources and (era 7 local retail) grades changed. Each era's residual was added as a new SCALE claim. Era 1's residual took e1-scale-017 rather than e1-scale-015, because the era-1 source hunt has six unmerged pure transcriptions queued at e1-scale-015, e1-scale-016, e1-buyers-009, e1-buyers-010, e1-buyers-011 and e1-sellers-007; 015 and 016 are reserved for them. Era 5's residual took e5-scale-014 and era 7's took e7-scale-010, both the next free ID in their era.

pools.source_verdict: NO SOURCE FOUND, recorded as a completed exhaustive search rather than an open gap. Eleven named dead ends were closed: Census of Manufactures printing and publishing bulletins 1879-1919; HSUS T 485-491 and Millennial De516-522 (both start 1928, both Media Records Inc., trademark filed Nov 1928); Coen via Galbi; ANCAM (1920); PIB (1945); SRDS (1919, rates not spend); NAA (1950 on); the Library of Congress historical marketing data inventory; and Printers' Ink 4 May 1911, which has no classified line among its twelve channels. The two routes that would separate them run in OPPOSITE directions, and the pools are built from partly shared inputs, so their errors are negatively correlated: raising one mechanically lowers the other. Two of three lenses declared this pair unrankable and the third ranked it at only about 85 percent. Intervals [11,46] and [8,30] overlap across almost their whole length. The separating quantity is unmeasurable from any surviving source: how much of the Printers' Ink farm-and-mail-order line is periodical space bought by national brands versus outlay by mail-order houses, a $0-85m swing larger than the 6-point gap between the centrals.

Carried as unranked because the reference-class lens declared it indeterminate with high confidence and the intervals overlap over their whole range. findings: The apparent 17-to-36 percent spread across the lenses on national_brand is NOT a measurement disagreement. It is a denominator-treatment disagreement, and on the channel-enumerated basis the lenses agree to within 1.5 points on every pool: structural-proxy 26.8 / 38.0 / 3.7 / 22.5 with 9.0 unassigned, decomposition 27.9 / 36.6 / 4.0 / 23.0 with 8.6 business-and-notices.

The chapter should publish the CHANNEL-ENUMERATED partition as the primary figure and the benchmark-basis shares as a footnoted secondary line; all three lenses recommended this independently. Reconciled channel-basis split for 1914 on a $700-725m denominator: national_brand 27.9, local_retail 36.6, classified 3.7, direct_response 23.0, business-to-business and notices 8.8, summing to 100.0. RISK IF IGNORED: splicing era-1 benchmark-basis shares to era-2 Coen-basis shares on one chart crosses an undocumented redefinition worth a factor of about 1.65-1.72.

The 1.5187 Coen-to-Census wedge is an AVERAGE across money types and must be applied asymmetrically: above 1.5187 for national brand (implied display-only wedge about 1.58), roughly 1.15-1.25 for local retail placed direct with the paper, and 1.00 for classified, which carried neither agency commission nor cost of preparation. Applying the full wedge to classified, as the superseded record did, inflates that pool by roughly half and gets the DIRECTION of the receipts-to-outlay adjustment backwards.

The residual is a property of the evidence, not a research failure - but it is 37.8 percent, and it must be published as an explicit labelled line. Only 5-9 points is a real fifth money type; the other 29-33 points is the undocumented gap between a contemporaneous enumeration and a retrospective benchmark. Drawing the second as a money type would be a fabrication; hiding it would be worse.

ID COLLISION WARNING, now handled: the era-1 source hunt has six unmerged transcriptions queued at e1-scale-015, e1-scale-016, e1-buyers-009, e1-buyers-010, e1-buyers-011 and e1-sellers-007. This apply step reserved 015 and 016 and put the residual at e1-scale-017.

A source-provenance mystery in the era-1 notes is closed: the rejected 'Lineage C' figure ($600m for 1910, from Duke, uncited) is traceable to the Printers' Ink 4 May 1911 tabulation of $616m. The other half of that lineage, '4 percent of national income', stays rejected.

Three lines in the panel's builds are documented ASSUMPTIONS with no source of any kind and total roughly $113m, or 9.4 percent of the benchmark: window display and store signage (about $22m, in none of the twelve Printers' Ink channels), non-store local advertisers such as theatres, banks, hotels and physicians (about $43m), and the long tail of about 40,000 small mail-order and coupon advertisers (about $48m). Removing all three drops the four-pool sum by about 9 points and raises the residual correspondingly.

Highest-value next source, and it is free: walk the Printers' Ink run at the Internet Archive by date through 1912-1917 for a later edition of the 4 May 1911 channel table. A 1914 or 1916 edition would put a by-channel tabulation on the era's own benchmark year, test the x1.131 growth factor every lens used, and might carry a classified line. Second, identify the compiler of the 1916 Chicago all-eight-dailies display-versus-classified linage report Field describes. Third, and cheapest: read the 52-city classified LINAGE share for 1950 out of HSUS T 485-486 against the NAA 1950 revenue share of 18.2 percent already in the dataset - together they give the rate ratio r directly, and r sets the classified interval's width.

Two ceilings on knowability belong in the chapter. First, national_brand and local_retail cannot be separated at all. Second, the LEVEL of all four pools rests on a denominator that is a retrospective reconstruction running 1.72x the only contemporaneous tabulation, produced by the same publishing house, with no reconciliation ever documented. Shares WITHIN the measured base are far better identified than shares of total outlay, and no independent aggregate - tax, census or national accounts - can ever validate an era-1 money-type pool.

Directional continuity against era 2 holds on all four pools and was not used as an input to any build. Era 2's own 1949 reading is national 43, local 36, classified 6.5, direct response 14.5; the reconciled 1914 channel-basis reading is 27.9 / 36.6 / 3.7 / 23.0. Four out of four directions of travel match what the mechanism history predicts.
eras.buyers_grade_note: Era 1's BUYERS pools are not four restatements of the SCALE pools. e1-buyers-005 and e1-buyers-006 stay grade B, because they are transcriptions of the ANPA newspaper national/local dollars rather than constructions, and the reconciliation changed only their provenance flag. e1-buyers-007 (classified as a share of newspaper receipts) and e1-buyers-008 (the direct-response buyer pool in dollars) are grade C constructions and carry the full route-by-route method.

observed_total.verified: Recomputed from adspend.json series.coen_mce.points where partition_member=true; the 11 medium lines sum to exactly 247,472. Full era path re-confirmed: 1994 153,024 / 1995 162,930 / 1996 175,230 / 1997 187,529 / 1998 206,697 / 1999 222,308 / 2000 247,472 / 2001 231,287; era cumulative 1,586,477.
observed_total.basis_caveat: Advertiser billings valued at list price, bottom-up, 11 media. Every share below is conditional on this basis. The direct-mail basis question is larger than every interval in the table.

eras.route_consolidation: About fourteen named routes across three lenses collapse to eight independent evidence bases. The Coen national/local geography residual was offered seven times, MAGNA via Statistical Abstract T1279 six times, the 1997 Economic Census three times, DMA/WEFA three times with three different discount factors, the Knight Ridder 10-K three times, and IAB format and pricing shares five times. Genuinely distinct and offered once each: USPS postal quantities, the ERA/infomercial direct-response-TV build, the PIB 1993 magazine mail-order category, and the demand-side buyer-count fringe build. CONSEQUENCE: national_brand and local_retail rest on TWO independent evidence bases plus one one-year, one-medium official check.

residual.unit: percentage points of the observed 2000 US total; negative means the four pools over-allocate
residual.cause: An exact, fully attributable artefact of the median operator. The medians for national_brand (38.34), local_retail (28.32) and direct_response (24.71) all come from the Fermi lens, whose own four values sum to 100.00 with classified at 8.63; the classified median is 8.85, from the reference-class lens, and 8.85 - 8.63 = 0.22 exactly.
residual.bounds: Taking the mean of lens centrals instead of the median reconciles to 100.000 exactly, and dropping any one lens and taking the mean of the remaining two reconciles to within 0.003pp.
second_larger_residual_outside_the_unive: TELEMARKETING: DMA counts $73.2bn of it as advertising in 2000; Coen counts none. That is 29.6 percent of the observed total, and if it were in the denominator direct response would dominate every other pool. A scope choice, not a measurement error.

ONLINE LISTING AND POSTING REVENUE: Forrester put the whole US online recruitment market at $1.2bn in 2000, more than double IAB's entire classifieds format ($566m); a bottom-up build from named sellers puts real online classified near $1.0bn against the $455m that fits inside Coen's internet line. Roughly $0.5-1.0bn of functionally classified money sits outside every series here.

1994 HAS NO DIRECT-RESPONSE SOURCE OF ANY KIND: the WEFA series begins in 1995 and 1994 is backcast at the published 1995-2000 medium-weighted CAGR of 8.69 percent. That year should render as a visible hole, not a point.

findings: THE REVISION IS UNANIMOUS IN DIRECTION. Every lens moved intent money up. Standing: classified 8.2 + direct_response 19.2 = 27.35 percent of the 2000 market, $67.7bn. Reconciled: 8.85 + 24.71 = 33.56 percent, $83.1bn - a $15.4bn, 6.21pp revision. The lowest lens central for direct_response (22.62) is still 3.4pp above the standing figure. Independent corroboration: re-expressing MAGNA's own Direct share with Coen's direct-mail line, changing nothing else, gives 28.2 percent, and MAGNA's Direct excludes direct-response TV, print and radio and telemarketing by construction. The standing 19.2 percent was nine points below another compiler's floor.

THE SHARE PEAK PRECEDES THE DOLLAR PEAK BY THREE YEARS, AND THIS IS GRADE B, NOT C. Newspaper classified's share of US advertising peaked in 1997 at 8.944 percent and fell every year after, while dollars kept climbing to the 2000 peak of $19,608m. Any migration chart dated at the 2000 dollar peak is dating the wrong quantity for a share-based argument, and the 1997-1999 slide is a denominator effect a naive chart will misattribute to search.

THE DIRECT-MAIL BASIS IS A CEILING ON KNOWABILITY, AND IT IS LARGER THAN EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS TABLE. Direct mail is 18.02pp of the observed 2000 total on its own. Coen books it at full advertiser program cost ($44,591m) while every other Coen medium is space only; MAGNA books the same medium and year at $18,250m, a 2.44x gap; USPS Standard Mail (A) postage was roughly $15-16bn. On a media-space-only basis the 2000 total falls to about $221bn and the shares become roughly national_brand 43.6, local_retail 33.1, direct_response 13.4, classified 9.9. The rank order survives; the magnitudes do not. This is the only like-for-like basis on which era 5 can be compared with era 7's ex-direct-mail rail.

THE MEASUREMENT SYSTEM IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO EXACTLY THE MONEY THAT IS MIGRATING. Bottom-up from named sellers, real US online classified in 2000 was roughly $1.0bn (recruitment about $550m, automotive about $240m, real-estate listings about $150m, personals and portal sections about $60m). IAB's published classifieds line is $566m and only $455m fits inside Coen's smaller internet line. Pure-play job boards, auto portals and property portals sold direct to HR departments and dealers with no agency in the loop, and much of their revenue was job-posting and resume-database fees neither IAB nor Coen counted as advertising.

TWO INDEPENDENCE FAILURES COLLAPSE THE APPARENT CORROBORATION. DMA/WEFA's direct-mail line matches Coen to $9m and MAGNA's newspaper line matches NAA to $1m. Both are re-badged, not independent, on those media. The four compilers that appear to triangulate the two largest lines in this era are, on those lines, two.

THE GENERAL-MEDIA DIRECT-RESPONSE QUANTITY IS THE PANEL'S LIVE DISAGREEMENT, AND THE INDEPENDENT CHECKS LAND LOW. The panel spans $5.0bn to $18.5bn, 5.4pp of the market. The only published measurement (DMA/WEFA) says $104.2bn, which all three lenses reject. The two genuinely independent checks both land near the bottom: the ERA/infomercial build gives $3.5-5.3bn of direct-response television against DMA's $21.9bn, and PIB's 1993 magazine mail-order category was 9.8 percent of Coen magazines against DMA's 56.6 percent. No lens was discounted, because the high lens's figure is a disclosed and argued discount of a published measurement rather than a specification error.

VINTAGE INSTABILITY NOBODY WAS CARRYING. Coen restated Total National for 2000 by +2.41 percent and the internet line by +50.2 percent between the contemporaneous 2001 vintage and the Galbi-curated vintage. MAGNA restated its own 2000 direct mail by +10.0 percent between two consecutive Statistical Abstract editions. Running the identical construction on the 2001 vintage moves national_brand by about 0.9pp. Both instabilities are inside the reconciled intervals; neither was inside any point estimate the project carried.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE THESE NUMBERS, in order of value: (1) USPS Revenue, Pieces and Weight FY1994-2001, which settles the direct-mail basis at grade A; (2) a project-wide editorial rule on directories, which resolves 4.50pp and one of the three unranked pairs; (3) summing the roughly fifteen public newspaper groups' 10-Ks, which lifts the classified spine from B to A; (4) recovering MAGNA's licensed 1994-1999 backcast.

observed_total.unit: USD millions (current), US total advertising spend, 2025
observed_total.rail: MAGNA media-owner advertising revenue. Digital pure players $294,000m + traditional media owners $104,000m sums exactly, so DIRECT MAIL IS OUT of this rail. All four pools are defined ex-direct-mail to match, which is the fix for the mechanical residual depression the era-7 verifier flagged.
observed_total.note: The era record's e7-scale-001 carries $405bn as a MAGNA/EMARKETER blend, 1.8 percent above the observation and inside its own interval, so it is not a competing measurement. Reconciliation is on $398bn. The reference-class lens built its shares on $405bn; its shares are taken as stated rather than rebased, and the rebasing sensitivity is quantified in the residual.

pools.source_verdict: NO SOURCE. No compiler publishes a US national-brand advertising figure for any year after 2007. Partial free evidence exists only for 2008-2010 (Census SAS national/regional air time, grade A) and for newspapers to 2012 (NAA). The two instruments that would source the pool - Guideline/SMI agency billing data and MAGNA's National domain inside MG8 - are licensed and were not purchased.
pools.unit: percent of US advertising spend, 2025, MAGNA media-owner rail ($398bn, direct mail excluded)
pools.interval_source: min lower to max upper across the lenses, NOT route dispersion: routes N-A and N-B share the performance-share input. The lower end is where the independent survey rail (WARC/Ebiquity, adjusted, about 22 percent) sits; the upper end is where local_retail's lower bound pushes the residual.
pools.correction_size: The record read $95bn / 23 percent and called this the smallest of the four pools. Restated to $145.7bn / 36.6 percent: the pool is the largest or joint-largest. Two named causes, confirmed independently by all three lenses: the residual was computed with direct mail excluded from the denominator but present in two subtracted pools (about +6pp), and the local pool subtracted from it was an inventory-geography measure (about +11pp).

pools.source_verdict: POOL NOT SOURCED; ONE INPUT SOURCED AT GRADE A. IAB/PwC's 'Revenues by pricing model' exhibit publishes the performance-priced share of US digital annually 2004-2019 (57 percent for 2008, 62-66 percent across 2010-2019, 62.1 percent at HY2019), which converts the standing 'two-thirds is performance-priced' assumption into a published number for twelve of the nineteen era years. The exhibit was discontinued after HY2019, so 2020-2026 is extrapolation. The only source that ever sized the whole pool, DMA/IHS ($153.3bn in 2010, 54.2 percent of US ad expenditure), died inside the era.
pools.unit: percent of US advertising spend, 2025, MAGNA media-owner rail ($398bn, direct mail excluded)
pools.interval_source: min lower to max upper across the lenses, deliberately NOT the 4.2pp lens dispersion, which is spuriously tight because all three centrals are three parameterisations of the same unobserved quantity (the performance-priced share of US digital in 2025, set at 60.0, 62.6 and 67.7 percent).
pools.correction_size: Record read $130bn / 32 percent. Restated to $151.2bn / 38.0 percent. Path (b) of the standing method was retired as double-counting by construction; path (a) was rebuilt on the mutually exclusive format partition and re-anchored on IAB's published performance-priced share rather than an assumed two-thirds.

pools.source_verdict: NOT SOURCED AS A MONEY TYPE. BIA's $169bn US local advertising total measures a different object: BIA's own published definition is all media selling access to LOCAL AUDIENCES to ALL advertiser types INCLUDING national and regional companies - geography of inventory, not class of buyer. What IS available is BIA's own advertiser-type ratio, public in summary form at $116.4bn regional-and-national against $59.2bn SMBs (33.7 percent), corroborated by the BIA/Kelsey 2015 vintage at 35.9 percent. That ratio grades B; the derived 2025 pool needs a regional-tier allocation and a rail conversion on top of it, so the pool is C.
pools.unit: percent of US advertising spend, 2025, MAGNA media-owner rail ($398bn, direct mail excluded)
pools.interval_source: min lower to max upper across the lenses. The width is definitional, not statistical: BIA's regional-tier allocation alone spans it (0 percent gives 14.3, 45 percent gives 24.1).
pools.correction_size: Record read $169bn / 41 percent and made this the largest pool. Restated to $93.5bn / 23.5 percent - third on every lens. The largest single correction available in era 7, about 17pp of share, and it costs nothing.

pools.source_verdict: SOURCED FOR 2008-2021 AT GRADE A ON THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS - the hunt's main finding, which overturns the record's note that no modern source publishes this. (1) Census SAS NAICS 511110 classified advertising, free, 2005-2021: $8,087m (2008) to $1,978m (2021). (2) Census SAS NAICS 511140 directory advertising space, free, 2005-2020: $11,400m (2008) to $1,781m (2020), replacing two trade blogs. (3) IAB/PwC's classifieds line to 2021: $3.2bn (2008) to $5.3bn (2021). Overlap test passes: NAA $5,030m against Census $4,840m for 2011, 3.9 percent apart. NOT SOURCED: reference years 2022-2026 on any leg, and the marketplace and listings leg in every year, whose only specialist compiler (AIM Group) is a paid subscription that was not purchased.
pools.unit: percent of US advertising spend, 2025, MAGNA media-owner rail ($398bn, direct mail excluded)
pools.grade_note: The applied claim grade is C because the 2025 ANCHOR is unsourced: every sourced leg stops at reference year 2021. The 2008 anchor is fully grade A at $22.7bn and is recorded here so the sourced years are not left at C.
pools.interval_source: min lower to max upper across the lenses. WARNING: above about 2.8 percent the interval is FRAME, not measurement error - two lenses set their upper bound on a widened denominator ($410-421bn) that counts the listings successors. The two readings must never be blended in a chart.

scope_alternative.label: classified as a money type, listings-inclusive
scope_alternative.note: All three lenses independently reconstructed the listings leg and landed at $19.0bn, $21.0bn and $23.2bn gross. Indeed's US revenue alone ($5.31bn) approaches the whole of IAB's $12.5bn 'Other' bucket. This is the era-7 boundary-shift argument in one number.

pools.correction_size: Record read $15bn / about 4 percent, built by assigning the whole of IAB's $12.5bn 'Other' bucket to classified. Restated to $9.95bn / 2.5 percent, because lead generation is roughly $4.5-6bn of that bucket and is money paid per acquired lead.

residual.unit: percentage points of the $398bn observed 2025 US total; negative means the four pools over-allocate
residual.cause: The four medians sum to 100.6 percent, or $400.4bn. national_brand and direct_response are constructed complements - in every lens one is computed as, or against, the residual left by the other - so taking each pool's median independently picks national_brand from the reference-class lens and direct_response from the structural-proxy lens, a combination no lens produced. Each lens's own partition closes at 99.2, 100.0 and 100.0 percent.
residual.sensitivity: Rebasing the reference-class lens's dollar figures from its $405bn rail onto the observed $398bn and re-taking the medians gives 101.56 percent, a residual of -1.6pp / -$6.2bn: that is the interval's lower end. The upper end, 0.0pp, is reached if classified is taken at the structural-proxy lens's in-frame 1.9 percent and national_brand at the decomposition lens's 32.9 percent.
residual.outside_the_frame: Roughly $38bn of US direct mail (Winterberry $37.3bn for 2024) and roughly $12-16bn of classified-successor listing revenue sit outside the frame on BOTH sides of the ledger and are excluded from numerator and denominator alike.
residual.independent_second_reconciliation: Inside the digital sub-total the pools sum to $291.7bn against IAB's grade-A $294.593bn, a 1.0 percent gap.

unranked_pairs.lens_agreement: 3 of 3 lenses declare this pair unranked
unranked_pairs.reason: Centrals sit 1.4pp apart inside near-identical intervals, and the lenses do not agree on the direction: structural-proxy and reference-class order national_brand above direct_response, decomposition orders it below. The overlap is structural, not statistical - national_brand's dominant route is a residual computed after direct_response is subtracted, so the two move one-for-one. The independent instrument makes it worse: WARC/Ebiquity, adjusted, reads national_brand near 22 percent and direct_response near 57 percent, a complete reversal, and it cannot be dismissed because the pricing rail it contradicts has been unmeasured since HY2019.
unranked_pairs.resolvable_by: Guideline/SMI's national cut, or MAGNA's Direct/National/Local line items. Both licensed.

unranked_pairs.verdict: UNRANKED BY INTERVAL; direction unanimous but not certified
unranked_pairs.lens_agreement: all 3 lenses put national_brand above local_retail in their centrals, by 20.1pp, 13.1pp and 9.0pp, but they split on whether to certify it
unranked_pairs.reason: The combined intervals overlap over 25-31 percent, six points, so the pair is recorded as unranked rather than ordered. The dependence is the reason: national_brand is a residual and local_retail is the largest thing subtracted from it. The single input that decides it is BIA's regional tier - at 0 percent local_retail reads about 14.3, at 45 percent about 24.1, and at the decomposition lens's upper bound ($123bn) the ordering reverses outright.

unranked_pairs.verdict: UNRANKED AT THE TAIL ONLY; direction unanimous and wide
unranked_pairs.lens_agreement: all 3 lenses put direct_response above local_retail by 13.0pp, 18.4pp and 16.8pp
unranked_pairs.reason: Recorded for completeness: the combined intervals touch over 29.5-31 percent, about 1.5pp of shared range at the extreme tails. The ordering is supported but the intervals are not disjoint.

newly_ranked.verdict: RANKED. local_retail > classified, by roughly a factor of nine in frame and roughly a factor of four on the widest defensible classified scope.
newly_ranked.resolves: the source hunt's unranked_pairs_evidence entry 1 and gate-b-approval.md section 2's 'the middle two pools cannot be ranked'
newly_ranked.reason: 3 of 3 lenses rank this pair independently and decisively. Combined intervals [15.0,31.0] against [1.4,6.8] do not meet at any point, and they still do not meet if classified is taken on its listings-inclusive scope. The hunt was right about the cause and wrong that it was fatal: the pools were not disjoint, because BIA's PC/Laptop digital definition explicitly includes classified and vertical advertising. That is a stitching problem, not an evidence problem, and it lifts once the roughly $2-3.5bn of classified money inside BIA's local number is moved across.

newly_ranked.verdict: RANKED. national_brand > classified; intervals disjoint on every lens.
RANKED. direct_response > classified; intervals disjoint on every lens.

confidently_ranked.claim: classified is the smallest of the four pools, under every lens and every convention tested
confidently_ranked.reason: Its interval [1.4, 6.8] is disjoint from every other pool's, and remains so on the listings-inclusive scope.

grade_changes.reason: The only grade change in this stage that goes the wrong way, and it is required. The B grade rested on BIA's $169bn, a real published figure - but BIA's own definition makes it a measure of local-AUDIENCE INVENTORY sold to all advertiser types including national and regional companies. It is not a measurement of the local_retail money type, so it cannot carry a source grade for it. Central falls from $169bn to $93.5bn. NOTE: e7-buyers-006 already stood at C; only e7-scale-007 changes grade.

grade_changes.to: A for reference years 2008-2021; C retained for the 2025 anchor and for 2022-2026
grade_changes.applied: recorded, not applied to the claim grade
grade_changes.reason: The print-newspaper and print-directory legs are now sourced from official statistics (Census SAS NAICS 511110 and 511140), replacing the AEI Carpe Diem and Vendasta/UENI trade-blog citations, and IAB's own classifieds line to 2021 is the third leg. The 2008 anchor is fully grade A at $22.7bn. The APPLIED claim is anchored on 2025 and cannot inherit the upgrade, because every leg stops at reference year 2021 and nothing free covers 2022-2026 or the marketplace leg in any year. The period grades are recorded in the claim's method and in grade_by_period above, so the sourced years are not left at C.

grade_changes.direction: NO CHANGE to the pool; INPUT UPGRADE
grade_changes.reason: The pool has no source and stays C. But the method's central assumption - 'two-thirds of $294.6bn US digital is performance-priced' - is a PUBLISHED IAB figure for 2004-2019, not an assumption. The method now cites it and states explicitly that 2020-2026 is extrapolation across an exhibit IAB discontinued.

No source found; the residual construction stands and must stay one. What changes is the central ($95bn to $145.7bn) and the method, which now states the direct-mail treatment on both sides of the subtraction.

findings: THE RECORD'S ORDERING WAS WRONG AT THE TOP, and all three lenses reached that independently. The record made local_retail the largest pool at 41 percent and national_brand the smallest at 23 percent. On the reconciled split local_retail is THIRD at 23.5 percent and national_brand is joint-first at 36.6 percent. The single cause is that the record set local_retail equal to BIA's $169bn headline, whose own decomposition prices the national and regional leg at $116.4bn against $59.2bn for SMBs.

THE APPARENT AGREEMENT ON direct_response IS AN ARTEFACT, and it is the strongest argument in this era for the no-extremizing rule. All three centrals are three parameterisations of one unobserved quantity: the performance-priced share of US digital in 2025, extrapolated across the five years since IAB discontinued its pricing-model exhibit at 62.1 percent for HY2019. The lenses set it at 60.0, 62.6 and 67.7 percent.

THE ONE GENUINELY INDEPENDENT CONVERGENCE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE THREE-LENS AGREEMENT. Route D-B takes DMA/IHS's 2010 direct-marketing pool (54.2 percent of US ad expenditure), carries it forward, and converts it from a billings rail to the media-owner rail through the IRS SOI / MAGNA ratio of 1.456. It lands at 37.6 percent against the format rail's 38.5 percent, sharing no input. Separately, the reference-class lens rebuilt IAB's discontinued performance share from the FY2025 format partition with no fitting to the historical series and returned 62.6 percent against IAB's last published 62.1 percent - a five-year hole closed out of sample.

RAIL SENSITIVITY EXCEEDS EVERY INTERVAL IN THIS SPLIT. IRS SOI corporate advertising deductions read $473,153m for 2022 against MAGNA's $325,000m for the same year, a $148bn wedge, 45.6 percent of the MAGNA base. The wedge is trade and consumer promotion, co-op allowances, catalogue and mail production, agency fees and events, which is overwhelmingly direct-response and retail money. Carried to 2025 and allocated, every resulting shift is larger than the corresponding interval half-width: two lenses independently computed restatements putting national_brand near 29.5-31.8 percent and local_retail near 22.4-27.4 percent. Any chart of this split must name its rail in the axis label, not the footnote.

A CORRECTION TO THE SOURCE HUNT, on classified print. The hunt reports the record's roughly $1bn print-classified assumption as 'roughly half' the true value, citing Census's $1,978m for 2021. That compares a 2021 observation with a 2025 assumption. Carried forward four years at the observed -11 percent a year, $1,978m reads about $1.24bn by 2025, and two of three lenses independently landed at $1.15-1.3bn. The record's print assumption was approximately right FOR THE ANCHOR YEAR, and the hunt's correction, applied as stated, would inflate classified. The same date-alignment error applies to the directory leg.

A CORRECTION TO THE SOURCE HUNT, on BIA. The hunt records BIA's advertiser-type cut as paywalled and not purchased. Two of three lenses found a public summary giving $116.4bn regional-and-national against $59.2bn SMB. Only the RATIO is usable - the post is undated and its $175.6bn block does not reconcile with BIA's published 2018 local total of $151.2bn - which is exactly how all three lenses used it.

THE CLASSIFIED SPREAD IS ONE DEFINITIONAL FORK, NOT THREE ESTIMATES. Lead generation is roughly $4.5-6bn of IAB's $12.5bn 'Other' bucket. Two lenses move it to direct_response because money paid per acquired lead is action-priced; one keeps a portion at weight 0.35 because a firm paying per lead for a roofer is buying what the classified page sold. That single call produces almost the whole 1.9-to-3.4 spread.

THE SECOND DEFINITIONAL FORK IS DIRECTORIES, and it barely matters in 2025 but dominates 2008. Directory money is carried in classified here. The alternative - a plumber's directory listing is a local business buying advertising - moves classified from 2.5 to about 2.2 percent in 2025 but from 9.3 to about 5.2 percent in 2008, and moves local_retail up about 4pp in 2008.

THE ERA-OPEN (2008) SPLIT IS NOT RECONCILED, and cannot be against this repo's data: adspend.json carries no 2008 all-media total on any series (Coen ends 2007 at $279,612m, MAGNA begins 2018). The lenses disperse widely on the 2008 shares - national_brand 41-50, local_retail 23-28, direct_response 15-25, classified 6-11 - using two different reference years and two different direct-mail treatments. What IS solid at the era open is the classified dollar anchor, $22.7bn, buildable entirely from grade-A sources.

THE PANEL OFFERED FEWER INDEPENDENT ROUTES THAN IT APPEARS TO. After de-duplication the twelve pool-estimates rest on nine distinct routes, not the thirty-odd the lenses list. national_brand has only TWO construction routes and they share the performance-share input, plus one truly independent survey rail that all three lenses gave zero weight because it reads 15 points lower. local_retail is the strongest, with three genuinely independent routes whose SMB legs converged at $62bn, $63bn and $63bn.

THE FOUR PURCHASES THAT WOULD RETIRE THESE ESTIMATES, in the order all three lenses converged on: (1) BIA's advertiser-type cut, which resolves the regional tier; (2) Guideline/SMI agency billing data, the only instrument that could rank national_brand against direct_response; (3) AIM Group's Marketplaces Report, which replaces the filing-by-filing listings build; (4) MAGNA's Direct/National/Local line items, the only source that would give three pools on one internally consistent frame. Recorded so that the choice to estimate rather than buy is on the record.

FREEZE COMPLIANCE HOLDS. Every input across all three lenses carries a publication or reference date on or before 2026-06-30. BIA's 2026 forecast of $184.5bn and Winterberry's 2026 outlook are recorded by the lenses but not used, since the anchor year is 2025.

open_taxonomy_questions.title: Where does directory and Yellow Pages money sit? Era 5 splits it by advertiser geography; every other place in the project puts all of it in one intent pool.
open_taxonomy_questions.status: CLOSED at Gate B, 2026-07-30, by DECLARING A SEAM rather than by choosing a rule. Both taxonomies are now carried: see taxonomy_seam in this file. The magnitude, inconsistency and touch-list below stand as recorded and are the evidence base for the seam object.
open_taxonomy_questions.surfaced_by: the era-5 reconciliation (unranked_pairs entry 1) and an earlier R2b run; carried forward unresolved

magnitude.effect_on_era_5_shares: Local Yellow Pages alone is 4.499pp of the 2000 market. Under the era-5 convention local_retail leads direct_response 28.32 to 24.71; move the local leg across and direct_response leads 29.21 to 23.82. The flip is exact and this block is its sole cause.

open_taxonomy_questions.the_inconsistency: Era 5's e5-scale-011 and e5-scale-013 split directories by advertiser geography and are the ONLY place in the project that does. Three other places put ALL directory money in the intent pool: adspend.json's dataset-notes section 8 (the constructed intent grouping is newspaper classified $19,608m + the FULL $13,228m Yellow Pages line + direct mail $44,591m = $77,427m, recomputed exact and carried as ds-money_type-003); era 6's e6-scale-010 (the whole $14,250m Yellow Pages line, no split); and era 7's e7-scale-008 (classified and directories as one pool). MAGNA, the only compiler in the era-5 window that partitions by money type at all, also places ALL directories inside its Direct domain with no geographic split.
open_taxonomy_questions.why_not_resolved_here: Moving it would shift the project's most-quoted figure - the $19.6bn classified peak - into a headline pool and would ripple into series.naa_newspaper, ds-money_type-003, and chapters 01, 05, 06 and 09. No evidence in the 1994-2001 window adjudicates what a Yellow Pages buyer thought it was buying, so this is not resolvable by more research. It is an editorial rule, not a finding, and it belongs to the human at the freeze.
what_it_would_touch: p2-ad-market/data/eras/era-5.json: e5-scale-011, e5-scale-013, e5-buyers-011, e5-buyers-013 (and the SCALE/BUYERS summaries)
p2-ad-market/data/adspend.json: ds-money_type-003 ($77,427m intent grouping) and series.naa_newspaper's role as the classified spine
chapters 01 (the $77.4bn intent grouping), 05, 06 (the era-5 money-type table) and 09 (the four-era money-type table)
open_taxonomy_questions.recommendation_if_the_human_wants_one: Follow MAGNA, the data layer and eras 6-7: put all directory money in the response-and-listing pool in every era. That would make direct_response the second-largest era-5 pool and local_retail the third, and would remove the contradiction between era 5's claims and the project's own dataset notes. It would NOT change the classified pool in era 5, because directories would go to direct_response, not to classified. NOT TAKEN. The human's Gate B decision was to carry BOTH rules as a declared definitional seam, on the same footing as the Coen-versus-MAGNA basis break, rather than to prefer one and discard the other. The unified rule is the cross-era comparable basis; the geographic rule is era 5's native basis. See taxonomy_seam.

taxonomy_seam.title: Directory and Yellow Pages money, era 5: carried under BOTH taxonomies as a declared definitional seam
taxonomy_seam.status: DECLARED AND CARRIED, not resolved. Decided by the human at Gate B on 2026-07-30.
taxonomy_seam.decision: Do not pick one rule and discard the other. Era 5 keeps its geographic split as the era-native view and gains a sibling unified-intent split as the cross-era comparable view. This is the same treatment the dataset already gives the Coen-versus-MAGNA basis break: two internally consistent readings of the same money, both published, neither averaged away.
taxonomy_seam.supersedes: open_taxonomy_questions entry tax-01, which recorded this as OPEN and recommended picking the unified rule. The recommendation was NOT taken; carrying both is the decision.

geographic.label: era-native basis
geographic.rule: Split the Yellow Pages line by advertiser geography: local directory money is local money, national directory money is response money.
geographic.where_it_is_used: Era 5's own record and era 5's own chapter, at fields.SCALE.by_money_type and fields.BUYERS.by_money_type in p2-ad-market/data/eras/era-5.json.
geographic.argument_for: A plumber buying a quarter-page in the local Yellow Pages is a local business buying advertising in its own town, which is exactly what the local-retail pool is for. The directory salesman called on it door to door on a yearly contract, the same way the local newspaper rep did.

unified-intent.label: cross-era comparable basis
unified-intent.rule: Put ALL directory money in one intent pool - the response-and-listing pool - with no geographic split.
unified-intent.where_it_is_used: Everywhere else in the project, and it is therefore the basis every cross-era comparison must use: era 6 (e6-scale-010, the whole $14,250m Yellow Pages line), era 7 (e7-scale-008, classified and directories as one pool), adspend.json's intent grouping (ds-money_type-003, newspaper classified $19,608m + the FULL $13,228m Yellow Pages line + direct mail $44,591m = $77,427m), dataset-notes.md section 8, and MAGNA itself, the only compiler in the era-5 window that partitions by money type at all, which places all directories inside its Direct domain.
unified-intent.argument_for: A directory listing is bought to be found by someone already looking, and it is priced and renewed on the calls it produces. That is a counted reply, not reach. Overture's own 10-K benchmarked its business against Yellow Pages calls and direct-mail responses rather than against television.

taxonomy_seam.cross_era_comparable_basis: unified-intent. Any chart, table or sentence that sets era 5 beside another era must use it, because eras 6 and 7 and the dataset's own intent grouping are already built on it. Splicing era 5's geographic shares to era 6 or 7 crosses an undocumented redefinition worth 4.50 points of the 2000 market.
taxonomy_seam.era_native_basis: geographic. It is what era 5 reports on its own terms, and era 5's chapter states both rules and both orderings rather than presenting one silently.

local_retail.interval_note: The interval NARROWS from 12.2pp to 7.70pp rather than translating. The ceiling falls by the whole block, because the two lenses that set it carried the block inside this pool. The floor holds at 20.8, because 4.50pp of the native 7.52pp downside WAS the directory convention; settle it by rule and the 3.02pp that remains is the dispersion the lenses actually disagree about.

direct_response.interval_note: A pure translation, width unchanged at 17.0pp. The directory question contributes none of this pool's native width, which is the general-media direct-response quantity ($5.0-18.5bn, about 5.46pp) plus the basis gaps. A block that is either wholly out or wholly in adds no uncertainty of its own.

pools_that_do_not_move.national_brand: identical under both rules at 38.34 percent / $94,881m (e5-scale-010, e5-buyers-010). No directory money sits in it under either rule.

taxonomy_seam.no_evidence_adjudicates_it: Confirmed, and it is not a gap that more research closes. No source published in or about 1994-2001 records what a Yellow Pages buyer thought it was buying. Coen publishes one Yellow Pages line and splits it by advertiser geography, not by intent; MAGNA publishes it inside Direct and does not split it at all; no survey of directory advertisers' purchase intent exists for the window. The choice is therefore an editorial rule, not a finding, and no amount of source hunting can convert it into one. That is precisely why both rules are carried rather than one being preferred.

consequence_the_ordering.under_the_geographic_rule: local_retail LEADS direct_response, 28.32 percent to 24.71 percent ($70.1bn to $61.2bn). Local retail is the second-largest pool and direct response the third.
consequence_the_ordering.under_the_unified_rule: direct_response LEADS local_retail, 29.21 percent to 23.82 percent ($72.3bn to $58.9bn). Direct response is the second-largest pool and local retail the third.
consequence_the_ordering.cause: The flip is exact and the local Yellow Pages block is its sole cause. Nothing else in the two pools changes.
consequence_the_ordering.unranked_either_way: Under BOTH rules the two intervals still overlap - [20.8,33.0] against [19.0,36.0] on the geographic rule, [20.8,28.5] against [23.5,40.5] on the unified one - so the pair remains unranked by interval on either basis and a chart must not sort these two bars. What the rule decides is which central is larger, not whether the pair can be ranked.
consequence_the_ordering.unaffected_orderings: national_brand is first on the central under both rules, and classified is unambiguously last under both. Only the middle two pools swap.
